newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MATCHES IN ITALY'S SERIE A THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN ITALY'S SERIE A THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in Italy's serie A (All matches Sunday, kick-off times GMT):

Both sides have injury doubts about their number one strikers, Roberto Mancini of Sampdoria and Filippo Inzaghi of Atalanta, the latter on top of the goalscorers' list with 15. With just one point from their last three games, Sampdoria appear to have gone off the boil. Atalanta may take advantage.

Winners against Fiorentina last week, Lazio must fancy their chances despite the continuing absence of injured trio of striker Pier Luigi Casiraghi, Australian midfielder Paul Okon and Giorgio Venturin. Struggling Cagliari again look to the Uruguayan pair Dario Silva and Fabian O'Neill.

Fiorentina have clearly long ago opted to concentrate on their Cup Winners's Cup this season, with a 2-0 win over Benfica on Thursday night. The proximity of that match could favour in-form and full strength Bologna, winners at Sampdoria last week.

With 1-1 European midweek draws against Norwegians Rosenborg and Belgian side Anderlecht respectively under their belts, both sides come into this top of the table clash in good form. English midfielder Paul Ince is suspended which makes it likely Inter will play a three man attack of Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Maurizio Ganz in front of Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff. Juventus, again without Alessandro Del Piero and Croat Alen Boksic in attack, will be led by Michele Padovano and Christian Vieri.

How the mighty have fallen. This used to be Gullit versus Maradona, a potentially decisive title clash rather than a mid-table battle. Bouyant Italian Cup finallists Napoli will be without injured Brazilian Andre Cruz as well as Argentine defender Roberto Ayala and right back Mauro Milanese, both suspended. Milan again relegate Roberto Baggio to the substitutes' bench with Liberian George Weah partnered by Marco Simone in attack and Croat Zvonimir Boban and Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic returning alongside Demetrio Albertini and Frenchman Marcel Desailly in midfield.

Revenge could be in the air here when Perugia coach Nevio Scala finds himself facing Parma, the club he coached for the last seven seasons. Both sides will be missing key players through suspension, midfielder Carmine Gautieri for Perugia and defender Fabio Cannavaro and striker Enrico Chiesa for Parma.

Due to be played at the neutral venue of Bologna because Reggiana's ground is banned following incidents at their home tie with Parma two weeks ago, this relegation battle could see visitors Piacenza take a significant step towards ensuring first division survival at the expense of bottom club Reggiana.

Roma should confirm recent return to form at expense of second from bottom Verona. Argentine Abel Balbo and Francesco Totti lead the Roma attack while Verona rely on Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zannini.

With just one point from their last four games, one time league leaders Vicenza appear to have lost their way. Led by Roberto Murgita and Uruguyan Marcelo Otero, they may find it difficult to win against a useful Udinese side which fields a powerful attack of German Oliver Bierhoff and Paolo Poggi, with Brazilian Amoroso in reserve.
